title: Kingdom of Italy
wiki_lead:
The Kingdom of Italy was a unitary state that existed from 17 March 1861, when Victor Emmanuel II, King of Sardinia, was proclaimed King of Italy, until 18 June 1946, when the monarchy was abolished, following civil discontent that led to an institutional referendum on 2 June, resulting in the establishment of the modern Italian Republic. The kingdom was established through the unification of several states over a decades-long process, called the Risorgimento. That process was influenced by House of Savoy-ruled Sardinia, which was one of Italy's legal predecessor states.
In 1866, the Third Italian War of Independence broke out; it was part of the Italo-Prussian Alliance against the Austrian Empire. Upon victory, Italy received Veneto. Italian troops captured Rome in 1870, ending the more than one thousand years of Papal temporal power.
In the last two decades of the 19th century, Italy developed into a colonial power, resulting to the establishment of the Italian Empire in 1882; that year, it entered into the 'Triple Alliance' with the German Empire and the Austro-Hungarian Empire, following strong disagreements with the French Third Republic about their respective colonial expansions. Although relations with Berlin became very friendly, the alliance with Vienna remained purely formal, due in part to Italy's desire to acquire Trentino and Trieste from Austria-Hungary. As a result, Italy accepted the British invitation to join the Allies of World War I in 1915. Victory in the war gave Italy a permanent seat in the Council of the League of Nations, but it did not receive all the territories it was promised.
In 1922, Benito Mussolini became prime minister and the National Fascist Party took control of the Italian government, thus ushering an era of the Fascist period in Italy known as "Fascist Italy". Authoritarian rule was enforced, crushing all political opposition while promoting economic modernization, traditional values, and territorial expansion. In 1929, the Italian government reconciled with the Roman Catholic Church through the Lateran Treaties, which granted independence to the Vatican City. The following decade presided over the Spazio vitale, an aggressive foreign policy that launched successful military operations in the Second Italo-Ethiopian War in 1935, Italian military intervention in Spain in 1937, and the Italian invasion of Albania in 1939. This led to economic sanctions, departure from the League of Nations, growing economic autarky, and the signing of the Pact of Steel and Anti-Comintern Pact with Nazi Germany and the Empire of Japan.
Italy entered World War II as a leading member of the Axis powers in 1940, and despite initial success, was defeated in the North African campaign and the Eastern Front. The Allied invasion of Sicily led to the fall of the Fascist regime. The new government surrendered to the Allies in September 1943 at the Armistice of Cassibile. German forces occupying northern and central Italy established the Italian Social Republic (ISR) and reappointed Mussolini as dictator, opening the Italian Civil War, where the National Republican Army of the ISR and its German allies contended with the Allied forces and the Italian Co-belligerent Army and Italian resistance movement. Shortly after the Surrender at Caserta of all Axis forces in Italy, civil discontent prompted an institutional referendum, which established a republic and abolished the monarchy in 1946.

grok_lead: The Kingdom of Italy was a unitary sovereign state in Southern Europe that existed from March 17, 1861, when Victor Emmanuel II of the House of Savoy was proclaimed king following the unification of most of the Italian peninsula, until June 1946, when a national referendum abolished the monarchy in favor of a republic. Under the Savoyard dynasty, the kingdom completed its territorial unification by annexing Rome in 1870 after the Papal States' collapse, establishing the capital there and granting the monarch the title "King of Italy" with the ancient Iron Crown as a symbol of legitimacy. The state industrialized rapidly in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, entered World War I allied with the Entente powers in 1915, and expanded its colonial holdings in Africa, including Eritrea, Somalia, Libya, and later Ethiopia, forming what became known as the Italian Empire by the 1930s. During the interwar period under King Victor Emmanuel III, Prime Minister Benito Mussolini consolidated power after his 1922 appointment by the king, transforming the kingdom into a fascist regime that invaded Ethiopia in 1935, allied with Nazi Germany, and joined World War II on the Axis side in 1940, leading to military defeats, Allied invasion, and Mussolini's ouster in 1943. The kingdom's participation in the war and the monarchy's association with fascism contributed to its downfall, culminating in the 1946 referendum where voters narrowly chose republicanism amid regional divides, with southern Italy favoring retention of the crown; the House of Savoy was subsequently exiled.
